definitions.gloss: to become defiant; to brazenly stand one's ground
definitions.explanation: to stop apologizing and defiantly assert oneself, often when caught doing something wrong

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{非|ひ}を{認|みと}めず{開|ひら}き{直|なお}った。
examples.english: He wouldn't admit his fault and became defiant.

examples.japanese: {開|ひら}き{直|なお}って「{悪|わる}いか」と{言|い}った。
{謝|あやま}るかと{思|おも}ったら{開|ひら}き{直|なお}ってきた。
examples.english: I thought they would apologize, but instead they got defiant.

notes:
USAGE:
- {開|ひら}き{直|なお}る (to become defiant)
- {開|ひら}き{直|なお}って〜 (defiantly...)
Typically negative - describes someone who, instead of apologizing when confronted about wrongdoing, becomes boldly unapologetic or aggressive. Similar to 'doubling down' in English.

CAN BE POSITIVE:
Rarely, can describe someone who stops worrying about others' opinions and confidently moves forward.

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし})

RELATED WORDS:
- {居直|いなお}る (similar - to turn defiant, more aggressive)
- {逆|ぎゃく}ギレ (reverse anger - getting angry when confronted)
- {開|ひら}き{直|なお}り (noun form - defiance)

cross_references.label: to become defiant; to turn aggressive
